title: Member Services Training Notes: Default History and Agreement Frequency in Payment Arrangements Offers
content:
**Member services training — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): the history test applied before an offer**

**The rule.** Default history is read across the member's whole portfolio, while frequency is read per service account. An agreement may be offered only when the member's defaulted agreements counted in the lookback are at most the tier's number of prior defaults allowed, and the agreements accepted on the same service account in the rolling count are below the tier's number of agreements allowed in 12 months. A default on any of the member's service accounts counts against an offer on every other account of the same member. Expired offers count toward neither. Both counts are taken from the cooperative's arrangement records.

**How each count is taken**

| Count | Window | Records counted |
|---|---|---|
| Defaulted agreements of the member | the tier's default lookback, in calendar months, ending on the offer date | every agreement of the member, on any of the member's service accounts, in defaulted status whose end date falls in the window |
| Agreements accepted on the service account | the 365 days ending on the offer date | every agreement of the same service account whose accepted date falls in the window |

The tier's limits — prior defaults allowed, agreements allowed in 12 months and the default lookback — are those of the limits table of the Payment Arrangements tiers.

**Questions answered in training**

*Does a default on the member's shop meter account count when the member asks for an agreement on the home account?* Yes. Defaults are counted across every service account of the member, so a default on any one counts against an offer on every other.

*Does an agreement accepted on the member's other service account count toward the frequency limit of this account?* No. Frequency is counted only on the same service account.

*Does an offer that expired unaccepted count?* No. An expired offer was never accepted and never defaulted, and it counts toward neither test.

*Is the frequency test met when the count equals the tier's limit?* No. The accepted count must be below the limit. The default test, by contrast, is met when the defaulted count equals the number allowed.

**Worked check (hypothetical tier allowing 1 prior default and 2 accepted agreements in 12 months)**

| Defaulted agreements in the lookback | Agreements accepted on this account in the 365 days | History test met |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | yes |
| 1 | 1 | yes |
| 2 | 0 | no — defaults above the number allowed |
| 0 | 2 | no — accepted count not below the limit |
